title: Separate timer activation from job success
goal: Read a loaded oneshot service’s limits, identity and failure result, then retry only a private job and verify its actual output.
challenge: Create a uniquely named monotonic timer for a finite learner job. Observe a deliberate exit7 while the unit is loaded, distinguish the timer trigger from failed work, retain the failed script, repair a separate private script and verify learner-owned successful output. Stop only these named units.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/operations-timerresult.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/operations-timerresult.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command: here && fresh failed.sh job.sh limits.txt failed.txt timeout.txt result.txt uid.txt report.txt && unit=ll-ops-result-${w##*.} && test "$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p LoadState --value)" = not-found && test "$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.timer" -p LoadState --value)" = not-found && printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' 'umask 077' 'w='"'$w'" '/usr/bin/id -u > "$w/uid.txt" || exit 19' '/bin/sleep 2' 'exit 7' > failed.sh && cp -- failed.sh job.sh
steps.explanation: Refuse collisions; no existing unit or account is changed. This name belongs only to this recorded workspace.
steps.expected: Private two-second failing script; both unit names absent.

steps.command: timer_wait() { deadline=$((SECONDS+12)); until test "$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p ActiveState --value)" = activating; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" || return 19; sleep 0.1; done; sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p User -p Type -p TimeoutStartUSec -p MemoryMax -p TasksMax > limits.txt; until test "$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p Result --value)" = exit-code; do test "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" || return 19; sleep 0.1; done; sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p Result -p ExecMainStatus -p ActiveState > failed.txt; }; here && fresh limits.txt failed.txt uid.txt && sudo systemd-run --unit="$unit" --on-active=1s --timer-property=AccuracySec=100ms --property=Type=oneshot --property=User=learner --property=TimeoutStartSec=4s --property=MemoryMax=64M --property=TasksMax=16 --property=RemainAfterExit=yes /usr/bin/timeout -k 1s 6s /bin/sh "$w/job.sh" && timer_wait && grep -qx ExecMainStatus=7 failed.txt && grep -qx User=learner limits.txt && cat limits.txt failed.txt
steps.explanation: Read limits during execution, before transient collection. TimeoutStartSec bounds a oneshot start, not RuntimeMaxSec. The timer can fire even when the job fails.
steps.expected: Loaded User=learner, four-second start timeout,64MiB/16tasks; actual exit7.

steps.command: here && fresh timeout.txt && test -f job.sh && test ! -L job.sh && test "$(stat -c %U:%a:%h job.sh)" = learner:600:1 && printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' '/bin/sleep 6' > job.sh && { begin=$SECONDS; sudo systemctl restart "$unit.service"; rc=$?; elapsed=$((SECONDS-begin)); test "$rc" != 0 && test "$elapsed" -ge 3 && test "$elapsed" -le 8; } && sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p Result -p ExecMainStatus -p TimeoutStartUSec > timeout.txt && grep -qx Result=timeout timeout.txt && grep -qx TimeoutStartUSec=4s timeout.txt
steps.explanation: Exercise the real loaded oneshot timeout with one six-second child, no busy loop. Retain failure and elapsed time; guest root could change limits.
steps.expected: Actual Result=timeout after the configured four-second limit; finite child terminated.

steps.command: here && fresh result.txt report.txt && test -f uid.txt && test ! -L uid.txt && test "$(stat -c %U:%a:%h uid.txt)" = learner:600:1 && test -f job.sh && test ! -L job.sh && test "$(stat -c %U:%a:%h job.sh)" = learner:600:1 && test "$(cat uid.txt)" = "$(id -u)" && printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' 'umask 077' 'w='"'$w'" '/usr/bin/id -u > "$w/uid.txt" || exit 19' 'printf "TIMER_OK\n" > "$w/report.txt"' > job.sh && sudo systemctl restart "$unit.service" && sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p Result -p ExecMainStatus -p ActiveState > result.txt && grep -qx Result=success result.txt && grep -qx ExecMainStatus=0 result.txt && test "$(cat report.txt)" = TIMER_OK && test "$(stat -c %U:%a report.txt)" = learner:600 && test "$(cat uid.txt)" = "$(id -u)"
steps.explanation: A manual retry is deliberately separate from a new timer tick. Preserve failed.sh; verify status, output and identity, not merely an active label.
steps.expected: Successful learner-owned report, exit0; original failing script retained.

steps.command: unit_quiet() { load=$(sudo systemctl show "$1" -p LoadState --value) || return 19; if test "$load" = not-found; then return 0; fi; test "$load" = loaded || return 19; state=$(sudo systemctl show "$1" -p ActiveState --value) || return 19; case "$state" in inactive|failed) ;; *) return 19;; esac; main=$(sudo systemctl show "$1" -p MainPID --value) || return 19; control=$(sudo systemctl show "$1" -p ControlPID --value) || return 19; test "$main" = 0 && test "$control" = 0; }; stop_private() { here || return 19; test "${unit:-}" = "ll-ops-result-${w##*.}" || return 19; service_load=$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p LoadState --value) || return 19; test "$service_load" = loaded || return 19; service_user=$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p User --value) || return 19; test "$service_user" = learner || return 19; exec_start=$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.service" -p ExecStart --value) || return 19; printf '%s\n' "$exec_start" | grep -Fq "argv[]=/usr/bin/timeout -k 1s 6s /bin/sh $w/job.sh ;" || return 19; timer_load=$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.timer" -p LoadState --value) || return 19; if test "$timer_load" = not-found; then true; elif test "$timer_load" = loaded; then triggers=$(sudo systemctl show "$unit.timer" -p Triggers --value) || return 19; test "$triggers" = "$unit.service" || return 19; sudo systemctl stop "$unit.timer" || unit_quiet "$unit.timer" || return 19; else return 19; fi; sudo systemctl stop "$unit.service" || unit_quiet "$unit.service" || return 19; unit_quiet "$unit.timer" && unit_quiet "$unit.service"; }; stop_private
steps.explanation: Before Stop verify the exact service identity/path. A one-shot transient timer may already be collected: accept only a successful exact LoadState=not-found query; otherwise verify its target before Stop. Stop only these two names; never reset all failed units or delete unrelated units.
steps.expected: This private timer and service stopped; evidence remains.

hints: Inspect the associated service, not just the timer.
A timeout for Type=oneshot belongs to start; inspect while loaded.
review: I retained actual statuses, bytes and relevant identities, including the incorrect case; successful command exit alone is not my evidence.
I can explain the stated limitations and independently meet the Challenge outcomes. Completion records my self-review, not an automatic assessment.
I preserved originals and inspected the exact cleanup inventory before deleting only this recorded practice workspace.
